findings.issue_text: Migration calls .first/[0]['id'] on embed_category site_setting query result; if the setting was never set the row doesn't exist and execute(...)[0] is nil, causing NoMethodError and aborting the migration for most existing installs

embeddable_hosts_controller update and destroy load record with .where(id: ...).first but never check for nil, resulting in NoMethodError (500) instead of 404 for stale/invalid ids

In store.js.es6 _hydrateEmbedded plural branch, delete obj[k] executes unconditionally even when _lookupSubType returned nothing, silently dropping *_ids data; also .map will throw if obj[k] is not an array
save_host dereferences params[:embeddable_host][:host] without checking the embeddable_host key exists; malformed requests raise missing-key errors rather than 400
embedding_controller update performs no mutation yet is routed (PUT) and called by front-end saveChanges(), a dead/no-op API that misleads consumers into thinking settings were saved
Migration destructively removes embeddable_hosts and embed_category site settings via raw DELETE inside change, making it non-reversible by rollback; should be split/annotated
No index is added on the host column despite record_for_host querying it on every embed request
Controller specs only assert the controller's superclass; create/update/destroy actions (including validation failures and nil-record cases) are not covered by tests
Fabricator definitions swapped: category_fabricator.rb contains the embeddable_host fabricator and vice versa, working only accidentally and living in misleadingly named files

goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In store.js.es6 _hydrateEmbedded plural branch, delete obj[k] executes unconditionally even when _lookupSubType returned nothing, silently dropping *_ids data; also .map will throw if obj[k] is not an array

adjudication.rationale: In the updated `_hydrateEmbedded` in `store.js.es6`, the plural `_ids` branch does `obj[k].map(...)` without checking `obj[k]` is an array, so it will throw if the payload contains `*_ids: null` or a non-array value. Also, unlike the singular `_id` branch (which only deletes `obj[k]` when hydration succeeds), the plural branch always executes `delete obj[k]` even if `_lookupSubType` returns `null`/`undefined` for one or all ids, thereby dropping the original `*_ids` data and replacing it with an array that may contain `null` entries. This is a verifiable behavioral/correctness issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: save_host dereferences params[:embeddable_host][:host] without checking the embeddable_host key exists; malformed requests raise missing-key errors rather than 400

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host, the code does `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` and `params[:embeddable_host][:category_id]` without guarding that `params[:embeddable_host]` is present. If a request omits the `embeddable_host` key (e.g., malformed/empty JSON or wrong parameter nesting), `params[:embeddable_host]` will be nil and `[:host]` will raise a NoMethodError, producing a 500 instead of a controlled 400-style error response. This is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embedding_controller update performs no mutation yet is routed (PUT) and called by front-end saveChanges(), a dead/no-op API that misleads consumers into thinking settings were saved

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb`, the `update` action only does `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)` and never reads params or persists anything (no model updates, no SiteSetting changes). Yet routes include `put "customize/embedding" => "embedding#update"`, and the front-end controller action `saveChanges()` calls `this.get('embedding').update({});`, which will hit that PUT endpoint. This makes the PUT API a no-op and can mislead callers into thinking changes were saved.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration destructively removes embeddable_hosts and embed_category site settings via raw DELETE inside change, making it non-reversible by rollback; should be split/annotated

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` uses a `change` method but performs irreversible operations via raw SQL, including `execute "DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')"`. In Rails, `execute` inside `change` is not automatically reversible, so rolling back this migration will raise an `ActiveRecord::IrreversibleMigration` (and even conceptually, the deleted site_settings values cannot be restored). This is a verifiable non-reversibility/destructive change introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No index is added on the host column despite record_for_host querying it on every embed request

adjudication.rationale: The new `embeddable_hosts` table migration (`20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`) creates `t.string :host` but does not add any index on `host`. The model lookup used for request authorization (`EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` -> `record_for_host`) performs `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first`, which will require a table scan without a suitable index and is called from `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` on embed requests. So the diff introduces a frequently-used lookup without indexing support (and the `lower(host)` predicate would ideally need a functional index or normalized storage).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Controller specs only assert the controller's superclass; create/update/destroy actions (including validation failures and nil-record cases) are not covered by tests

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The added specs `spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb` and `spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb` each contain only one example asserting the controller inherits from `Admin::AdminController`. There are no tests exercising the new controller actions (`create/update/destroy` in `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController`, `show/update` in `Admin::EmbeddingController`), nor cases like missing records (`EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` can be nil) or validation failures (`host.save` false). This is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: cancel() in embeddable-host.js.es6 calls this.rollbackBuffer() but never resets categoryId, so re-editing a host after a canceled edit could show the previous unsaved category selection

adjudication.rationale: In `embeddable-host.js.es6`, `categoryId` is set in the `edit()` action each time editing begins: `this.set('categoryId', this.get('host.category.id'));`. After `cancel()` on an existing host, the component sets `editToggled` to `false`, so to re-enter edit mode the user must invoke `edit()` again, which overwrites any previously unsaved `categoryId` value. For new hosts, `cancel()` removes the host via `deleteHost`, so stale `categoryId` would not be reused. Thus the diff does not verifiably introduce the described issue.
